tagline: From the turquoise lake up the Oregon Trail.
intro: From the Utah line along Bear Lake, its water a turquoise blue from suspended limestone, US 89 runs up the valley through St. Charles and Paris, Mormon towns whose settlers thought they were in Utah until the survey of 1872, to Montpelier. There the byway takes up the Oregon Trail and follows US 30 over Georgetown Summit to Soda Springs.

Old US 30 goes on through Bancroft and down the Portneuf River valley to Lava Hot Springs and McCammon. Emigrants knew Montpelier as Clover Creek, and the hundreds of carbonated springs at Soda Springs were a landmark on their trail.

moments.title: Paris
moments.text: The Bear Lake Stake Tabernacle, a red sandstone church built between 1884 and 1889, seats about 1,400 people in a town of 541.

moments.title: Montpelier
moments.text: Butch Cassidy and two of the Wild Bunch took about $7,000 from the Bank of Montpelier in 1896, and it is the only bank he robbed that still stands, vault and all.

moments.title: Soda Springs
moments.text: In 1937 the town drilled for hot water for a pool and got a geyser of cold water and gas, which flooded downtown for weeks and now goes off on the hour.
